turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same n-i-p (regular) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I'll analyze the training data systematically, then evaluate each candidate against the patterns learned.

## Step 1: Extract Key Patterns from Training Data

### Substrate
- SLG | FTO and SLG | ITO dominate high-efficiency devices
- FTO slightly more common in top performers

### ETL patterns (high-efficiency correlates):
- **TiO2-c | SnO2-np** → 20.85% (highest!)
- **TiO2-c | PCBM-60** → 19.35%, 14.25%
- **TiO2-c | BaSnO3-np** → 18.9%
- **TiO2-c** (plain, with good HTL) → 18.73%, 18.63%, 17.66%
- **SnO2-c | PCBM-60** → 18.0%, 17.28%
- **TiO2-c | C60** → 17.2%, 15.44% (ITO)
- **ZnO-np | PCBM-60** → 18.115%
- **SnO2-c** → 16.9%, 16.085%, 14.72%, 12.42%
- **TiO2-c | TiO2-mp** → broad range, typically 10-18%
- **TiO2-c | Graphene-QDs** → 17.405%
- **TiO2-c | SnO2** → 17.47%

### HTL patterns:
- **Spiro-MeOTAD** is the gold standard — appears in virtually all top devices
- **PTAA** → strong performer (15.3%, 15.46%, 18.19%, 18.9%)
- **PCDTBT1** → 19.35%
- **PbS-QDs | Spiro-MeOTAD** → 18.63%
- **PMMA | Spiro-MeOTAD** → 18.01%
- **Graphene oxide | Spiro-MeOTAD** → 16.15%
- **P3HT** → moderate (8-12%)
- **none** → generally lower

### Back contact:
- **Au** → consistently best (low work function mismatch, ohmic contact to Spiro)
- **Ag** → good, slightly lower on average
- **MoO3 | Au** or **MoO3 | Ag** → good for ITO devices
- **Carbon** → moderate

### Deposition:
- **Spin-coating** (single or multiple steps) → dominant in high-efficiency
- **Spin-coating >> CBD** → good for nanostructured ETLs
- **Spin-coating >> Dipp-coating** → 20.85% (top!)
- **Co-evaporation** → 17.9% for all-evaporated stack

## Step 2: Evaluate Top Candidates

Let me focus on candidates with the most promising combinations:

**c005**: SLG|ITO, TiO2-c|PCBM-60, PCDTBT8, MoO3|Au, Spin-coating>>Spin-coating
- Mirrors the 19.35% device (TiO2-c|PCBM-60 / PCDTBT1 / MoO3|Au). PCDTBT8 is a variant of PCDTBT1 — same polymer family, similar HOMO alignment. This is the closest analog to the highest-efficiency non-SnO2 device. **Very high potential: ~18-19%**

**c017**: SLG|ITO, C60;PhIm|C60, TaTM|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm, Ag, Co-evaporation
- Mirrors the 17.9% all-evaporated device (C60;Phlm|C60 / TaTm|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm / Au). Ag instead of Au is slightly worse work function match but the stack is nearly identical. **~17-18%**

**c064**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|SnO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|SnO2-np ETL is the same as the 20.85% device (which used Dipp-coating). Here spin-coating is used — likely slightly lower film quality for SnO2-np infiltration, but the combination is still excellent. SnO2 has better band alignment with MAPbI3 than TiO2 (conduction band ~−4.0 eV vs −4.2 eV for TiO2, reducing interface recombination). Spiro/Au is optimal HTL/contact. **~17-20%**

**c045**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers, PTAA, Au, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|TiO2-nanofibers appears in training at 12.06% with Spiro-MeOTAD/Au. Replacing Spiro with PTAA typically boosts efficiency (PTAA has better hole mobility, fewer pinholes). PTAA on FTO/TiO2-mp systems reaches 15-18%. The nanofiber morphology improves contact area. **~15-17%**

**c068**: SLG|ITO, SnO2-np|TiO2-np, PTAA, Au|MoO3, Spin-coating
- SnO2-np|TiO2-np bilayer ETL — SnO2-np alone gives 13.45-18.19% with Spiro; with PTAA (better HTL) and Au|MoO3 (good ohmic contact), this should be competitive. The bilayer provides complementary band alignment. **~16-18%**

**c073**: SLG|ITO-HMDS Scaffold, TiO2-c|C60, PTAA, Ag, Spin-coating
- TiO2-c|C60 with PTAA on ITO. Training shows TiO2-c|C60/Spiro/Ag = 17.2%, TiO2-c|C60/PTAA/Ag on ITO should be comparable or better (PTAA superior to Spiro in many ITO architectures). HMDS scaffold improves wettability. **~16-18%**

**c025**: SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|TiO2-np, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating>>CBD
- SnO2-c|TiO2-np bilayer. Training: SnO2-c|TiO2-c/Spiro/Au = 16.54%. With Ag instead of Au and CBD step, slightly lower. **~15-16%**

**c021**: PEN|ITO, SnO2-np|CPTA, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- CPTA is a self-assembled monolayer passivator for SnO2. SnO2-np alone on PEN|ITO gives 13.435%. CPTA passivation of SnO2 surface reduces interface recombination significantly. **~15-17%**

**c080**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c|MPMIC60, Spiro-MeOTAD, Ag, Spin-coating
- MPMIC60 is a fullerene derivative used as ETL interlayer — similar to PCBM-60 modification. TiO2-c|PCBM-60/Spiro/Ag = 14.25%. MPMIC60 is a methano-pyrrolidine modified C60, good electron extraction. **~14-16%**

**c013**: SLG|FTO, TiO2-c, P(VDF-TrFE)|Spiro-MeOTAD, MoO3|Ag, Spin-coating
- P(VDF-TrFE) is a ferroelectric polymer used as a dipole interlayer to improve Voc. Training: TiO2-c/IEICO-4F|Spiro/MoO3|Ag = 18.965%. The ferroelectric interlayer can boost Voc by ~50-100 mV. **~16-18%**

**c031**: SLG|FTO, SnO2-c|SnO2-mp|TiO2-c, Spiro-MeOTAD, Au, Spin-coating
- Triple ETL stack. SnO2-c|TiO2-c = 16.54%; adding SnO2-mp intermediate layer improves morphology and band cascade. **~16-17%**

## Step 3: Ranking the Top 5

Consolidating the analysis:

1. **c005** — TiO2-c|PCBM-60 / PCDTBT8 / MoO3|Au on ITO: direct analog of 19.35% champion, PCDTBT polymer family is proven, bilayer ETL passivates TiO2 surface, MoO3|Au ohmic contact. **Predicted ~18-19%**

2. **c064** — TiO2-c|SnO2-np / Spiro-MeOTAD / Au on FTO: same ETL as 20.85% record device, spin-coating slightly less optimal than dip-coating for infiltration but still excellent; SnO2 superior electron selectivity, Spiro/Au ideal hole contact. **Predicted ~17-19%**

3. **c017** — C60;PhIm|C60 / TaTM|F6-TCNNQ;TaTm / Ag, Co-evaporation on ITO: near-identical to 17.9% all-evaporated device, Ag vs Au minor penalty, PhIm vs Phlm minor variant. **Predicted ~17-18%**

4. **c013** — TiO2-c / P(VDF-TrFE)|Spiro-MeOTAD / MoO3|Ag on FTO: ferroelectric dipole layer boosts Voc, TiO2-c is proven ETL, MoO3|Ag good contact; training shows similar stacks reaching 18-19%. **Predicted ~16-18%**

5. **c068** — SnO2-np|TiO2-np / PTAA / Au|MoO3 on ITO: SnO2-np proven to 18.19% with PTAA, bilayer ETL improves electron extraction cascade, Au|MoO3 excellent ohmic contact. **Predicted ~16-18%**

---

**Final: c005, c064, c017, c013, c068**
